$description: Common: the raw palette, spacing, radius, motion, type and the floor marks that both kits use. Edit tokens here only; scripts/build-tokens.mjs generates everything else.

slate.$description: The main background. Centre of the radial ground behind WaveBackground, and the page colour wherever the background is not drawn.

slate-deep.$description: Edge of the radial ground: radial-gradient(120% 90% at 50% 40%, slate, slate-deep). Also a darker surface on slate (1.2:1, so give it a border if it must read as separate).

navy.$description: Accent 1: the navy glow bands. Light, not ink: 1.5:1 on slate, so never use it for text or a control's only boundary.

green.$description: Accent 2: the green glow bands. Also usable as an accent mark or text on slate (6.7:1) and slate-deep (8.3:1).

needs-you.$description: The one colour that means something needs you, in both kits: the light that rises from each step that leads to the thing, the point by “1 needs you”, the agent waiting on you. Change it here and every needs-you mark follows. Today the accent green (PDR-015); 6.7:1 on slate. Never a state colour, never focus.

floor-you-high.$description: Floors: the upper glow bands on your own floor. The same as green.

floor-department-high.$description: Floors: the upper glow bands on a department's floor, lavender. Also the department mark on the floor gauge (6.1:1 on slate).

floor-team-high.$description: Floors: the upper glow bands on a team's floor, warm amber. Also the team mark on the floor gauge (6.9:1 on slate).

floor-org-high.$description: Floors: the upper glow bands on the org's floor. Also the org mark on the floor gauge (5.1:1 on slate).

ink.$description: Text over the background, on slate (8.8:1) and slate-deep (10.8:1). Taken from the tuner panel's text colour.

ink-muted.$description: Secondary text on slate (5.1:1) and slate-deep (6.3:1). Taken from the tuner panel's muted colour.

surface-pane.$description: Level 1. The flat working plane content sits on: a list, a document, a table, a run log. Blurs the water behind it. ink on it is 7:1 or better even over the brightest band; ink-muted can fall to about 4.3:1 over a bright band, so keep it to 13px+.

surface-raised.$description: Level 2. One thing lifted off the pane or the water: a card, a sheet. Blurred, with a soft shadow (shadow-raised).

surface-inset.$description: Recessed inside a pane or raised surface: a preview, a quote, a draft. No border, no shadow.

surface-overlay.$description: Level 3. A decision over everything, such as an approval. Always on a veil; never more than one.

surface-bar.$description: Solid strips, such as an app bar if one is ever needed. Opaque, no blur. The shell's band and Title's letterbox are never solid: they use scrim.

scrim.$description: The fade the shell's chrome rests on, so its words stay readable over bright water or an app: under the top band, and Title's letterbox top and bottom. Always a gradient from this to transparent, never a block.

veil.$description: Darkens the water (and anything on it) to bring one thing forward. Used behind Glance and overlays, as a radial fade from about 35% at the centre.

hairline.$description: 1px borders on surfaces and dividers between rows. Decorative only.

hairline-strong.$description: Outlines that must be seen: pills, chips, the ask line at rest.

well.$description: The inside of a field, a box or a switch (Well): a slot a key sits in, a step darker than the ground.

well-edge.$description: A well's top line, drawn thicker: its depth, the way a key's is its bottom line.

scrollbar.$description: The thumb of a scroll bar. Avoid anything needing to scroll; where something must, its bar is thin and drawn in this, never the browser default.

danger.$description: Danger: things that can’t be undone. The Danger button’s outline, mark and armed fill; error text. 4.7:1 on slate, 5.8:1 on slate-deep; slate-deep on it is 5.8:1.

warning.$description: Warning: something needs care but nothing is broken (a sync is stale, a run is slow). 7.7:1 on slate. Never on buttons.

success.$description: Success: something finished well (sent, saved, done). Suggested: a yellower green than the accent, so “done” never reads as “look now”. 7.4:1 on slate. Never on buttons; the accent green stays the action colour.

info.$description: Information and focus: the industry blue, at the step that reads on dark (blue-500 #3B82F6 is only 3.5:1 on slate). Neutral notices and links. 5.1:1 on slate.

focus.$description: The keyboard focus ring and the focused input’s underline. Always info blue, so focus never looks like an action (green) or a state.

light.$description: Specular light on glass: Bubble highlights and the glint on a focused bubble. Never text, never a fill.

shade.$description: Shadow and masks: the darkness under raised things and overlays, and opaque stops in mask gradients. Never text.

effect.$description: The Calm Tide (default) values for the glow. Variants carry their own; see WaveBackground.

surface-blur.$description: Backdrop blur on panes, raised surfaces and overlays.

pattern-unavailable.$description: The fine hatching on something unavailable (a Signal's shadow, an action that can't be taken): it stays where it is and looks closed, and its words say why. A background, never the only cue.

radius.$description: Corners. The water and panes are soft; controls are pills.

radius-key.$description: Keycaps, source numbers, small number keys: the smallest rounded things.

radius-control.$description: Buttons: a key's corners (PDR: Keycap button). Soft enough to read as something to press, square enough to stay flat.

radius-card.$description: Panes, raised cards, overlays, sheets (top corners only).

shadow.$description: Panes are flat: no shadow. Elevation shows through blur and, from raised up, a soft shadow.

space.$description: Harry, from the Foundations Lab: golden-ratio steps on a 4px unit, snapped to 4px (4 × 1, 1.618, 2.618, 4.236, 6.854, 11.09, 17.94, 29.03). Values under 4px are geometry, not spacing.

space-1.$description: Inside a cluster that reads as one thing: a fact’s value to its label, chip padding, a menu item to its detail.

space-2.$description: Inside a control or a tight list: a keycap to its word, step rows, an eyebrow to a small title.

space-3.$description: Eyebrow to title, title to summary, row padding, an icon to its text.

space-4.$description: Between related blocks: a question to its answers, an icon to its heading, an inset inside a pane.

space-5.$description: Between groups: actions in a row, the facts on a card, padding beside a button’s label.

space-6.$description: Before the actions; padding inside panes, cards and overlays.

space-7.$description: Between sections; the gap between columns.

space-8.$description: The largest gap: section breaks on long pages, and space above a pane under the top band.

structure.$description: DRAFT. Where things go, how wide they get, and what sits over what. Measures: the five widths, always min(measure, 100% minus two gutters), centred on the axis. Anchors: fixed positions between the top and bottom bands. Layers: stacking order for whole components; inside one, use 0 to 3.

measure-glance.$description: A quick look, centred on the veil (Glance Veil).

measure-read.$description: The reading and asking column: the agent session, its ask line, a response.

measure-wide.$description: The widest thing on screen: a pane or a sheet. Two columns at most inside it.

measure-prose.$description: Longest line of running summary text inside any measure.

edge.$description: The gutter: chrome's distance from the left and right edges, and the minimum clear space either side of any container.

edge-tight.$description: The gutter below 640px wide, and either side of a sheet.

layer-view.$description: A full view (session, workspace, builder) over the menu.

layer-overlay.$description: An overlay on its veil: AgentApproval.

layer-chrome.$description: The top band: name and status stay visible over everything except the intro.

layer-toast.$description: AgentToast: the one thing allowed above everything.

target-md.$description: The height of a control people press: a button, a field. Enough for a finger as well as a pointer.

target-sm.$description: The height of a small control, in a toolbar or a row.

focus-ring.$description: The width of the focus outline every control draws when it has keyboard focus.

focus-gap.$description: The gap between a control and its focus outline.

key-edge.$description: A button's bottom line at rest: its depth, drawn as a line, never a shadow. Pressed, it closes to a hairline and the button sinks by the difference.

key-edge-sm.$description: The same bottom line on a small button.

well-depth.$description: A field's, a box's or a switch's top line (Well): how far it sits below the ground. A ticked box or an on knob comes up as a key with a bottom line this thick.

letterbox-ratio.$description: Urgent is letterboxed (PDR-009): the width-to-height ratio of the frame urgent and important things are shown in, the cinema's 2.39:1. Everything outside it steps back behind the scrim.

letterbox-min-frame.$description: The shortest a letterbox frame gets. On a small or narrow screen the frame holds this height rather than shrink its text to keep the ratio: legibility beats the ratio.

edge-rule.$description: The height of the edge rule at the top of the screen, where an urgent item waits (UrgentEdge) once it is stepped back from the letterbox. The same as space-5.

tracking.$description: Letter-spacing, as foundations. Capitals are always tracked; running text never is.

tracking-tight.$description: Large titles in normal case (title, display), pulled in slightly.

tracking-soft.$description: Small words that sit beside icons: presence labels, Bubble category names.

tracking-caps.$description: Capitals inside controls: every labelled button and suggestion pill.

tracking-label.$description: Small capital labels: eyebrows, fact labels, section labels, keys hints.

tracking-title.$description: The Title tier: chapter labels and the film-title type.

motion.$description: DRAFT. Durations and easing. Motion is slow and continuous on the water, quick and quiet on controls. Everything still works with reduced motion: things appear in place instead of moving. A token's $extensions.augur.reduced is its value under reduced motion, from the system (prefers-reduced-motion) or the page's own setting (data-motion="reduce" on <html>).

motion-instant.$description: Colour and opacity on hover: a word brightening, an outline appearing.

motion-quick.$description: Small things that answer a press: a menu opening, a row's actions appearing, a closing panel.

motion-base.$description: Most changes of state: a field's line, a toggle's track, the bulk bar, the veil.

motion-slow.$description: Something arriving: a dialog rising, a popover, the tide sliding a day, Search opening.

motion-calm.$description: A scene changing: the Shell's sky, a Glance, the menu stepping back.

motion-spin.$description: One turn of a working arc (a busy button, Running).

motion-run.$description: One pass of the hairline that runs under a busy field or a loading state.

motion-shimmer.$description: One sweep of a skeleton's shimmer.

motion-ping.$description: One ring of the ping: look now.

motion-still.$description: Kept for apps' own loops. The kit's loops stop under reduced motion instead, from the system or AUGUR's own setting.

motion-hold.$description: How long an Undo stays offered.

motion-drift.$description: Ambient loops that should never be noticed: the Bubble's iridescent swirl, an idle agent breathing. (The water runs on its own engine.)

travel-near.$description: How far a screen travels as it arrives or leaves: an app rising into place, sinking on Back. Under reduced motion nothing travels; it crossfades.

ease-standard.$description: Changes in place: colour, lines, fills.

ease-out.$description: Things arriving: they move fast, then settle. Dialogs, popovers, the tide.

ease-in.$description: Things leaving: they start gently and go.

ease-spring.$description: A small part settling with a touch of overshoot: a toggle's knob, a radio's dot. Never a panel.

ease-ping.$description: The ping's ring: out fast, fading slow.

font-sans.$description: The one sans, for all text and titles (PDR-015). Change it here, and the face in scripts/build-fonts.mjs, to change the kit's type.

font-mono.$value: "IBM Plex Mono", ui-monospace, Menlo, Consolas, monospace
font-mono.$description: The mono, for labels, small print, counts and code (PDR-015). Change it here, and the face in scripts/build-fonts.mjs, to change it.

type-label.$description: Eyebrows, fact labels, keycaps, section labels. Always uppercase and tracked, in ink-muted. Set uppercase.

type-small.$description: Back, notes, context lines, the clock's companions. The smallest normal-case text.

type-meta.$description: Details, rows, pills, steps, chips: the dense working text.

type-body.$description: Summaries, answers, buttons, options: anything read as a sentence.

type-lead.$description: The focused menu item, the ask line, a question: one line that leads.

type-heading.$description: View titles, an approval's question, the first line of an answer.

type-title-s.$description: Card and sheet titles, large fact values.

type-display.$description: The Split title: the one big word on a screen.

type-display-fluid.$description: Title-layout titles (letterbox). Uppercase, wide tracking, weight 200. Fluid: clamp(40px, 7vw, 80px) in CSS; shown here at its ceiling.

type-hero.$description: The intro wordmark only. Fluid: clamp(48px, 9vw, 112px) in CSS; shown here at its ceiling.
